7940.overview:
In this semi-FMV game you play a rookie facing his first game as starting quarterback on a fictional team, and this just happens to be The Big Game.

The entire game consists of this confrontation. When starting the game you watch a video of a kickoff and return, and then you get to select among 110 plays (100 passing and 10 running). The meat of the game is on the passing plays, where you are switched to a 3rd person behind-the-quarterback view from which you can see oncoming rushers. You can also zoom in on any receiver and via a targeting cursor make passes, or scramble if you don't find an open man.

Graphics consist mostly of FMV and super-imposed digitized images of no more than 320 x 200 pixels in resolution. There are also 6 difficulty settings to choose from.

11319.overview:
An enemy with the codename ''Quake'', which is believed to come from another dimension, is using teleporter gates to invade Earth. The player takes the role of a nameless soldier who arrives at his base only to find out Quake has overrun it and killed everyone. Somewhere in the base there must be a teleporter to Quake's realm. The mission is clear: take the fight to the enemy, overcoming countless hordes of monsters, and exact revenge.

id Software's followup to Doom and Doom II, Quake is a first-person shooter. Its main technological innovation is the use of a true 3D engine - the levels themselves as well as the enemies are polygonal. This not only allows for more natural level designs and character animations, but also for more realistic lighting and the inclusion of simulated physics that have an effect on gameplay: grenades can bounce off walls and around corners, for example.

In single-player mode, gameplay consists mainly of proceeding through the levels (spread over four distinct episodes) in search of an exit, killing everything that moves. Interaction with the game world is reduced to a minimum: since there is no use key, buttons are pressed by running into or shooting at them. As in id's earlier games, many secrets are waiting to be discovered, including a few hidden levels.

Unlike Doom's rather straightforward design that couples futuristic environments with demonic imagery, the theme of Quake's levels, enemies and weapons is not so easily pinpointed. While each episode begins in a futuristic military base (with a technological 'slipgate' as the level exit), later levels take place in environments inspired by medieval fantasy and gothic horror (castles, dungeons and caverns) and the player passes through magical portals to advance. In a departure from Doom's colorful environments, all Quake levels are dominated by earth colors.

The enemies conform to the mishmash of designs: there are human opponents armed with shotguns and energy weapons in the early levels, while the later levels include medieval knights, ghosts, zombies, ogres (armed with grenade launchers and chainsaws) and some more unearthly beasts. The player's weapons, while relatively modern, all have a low-tech feel. Besides a (bloodstained) axe, there are shotguns, nailguns, rocket and grenade launchers and the Thunderbolt, which discharges electrical energy.

Quake was one of the first games playable natively over the Internet in addition to LANs. The single-player levels can be played cooperatively, but the game is most famous for its deathmatch mode. One-on-one duels, team play and free-for-all competition are possible. The emphasis is on fast reaction and skillful maneuvering through the levels. All of the single-player maps can be used as arenas, but the game also comes with six maps especially designed for deathmatch.

157141.overview: Quantum Gate is an adventure game set on a distant planet, in which you are sent out to fight in a war with an alien race. Most of the game is played in a first person perspective, as you travel around your base and talk to other people. There are also fighting segments, done in FPS mode, in which you and your computer allies must battle alien soldiers.

157142.overview:
One night in Nijiiro Town, you look up and see eight meteors falling from the sky. One lands near you, and it turns out to be a small fairy. She tells you that the other seven meteors are a crystal that seals away a demon king in her world, split apart into pieces. These crystals have been found by seven girls throughout the town, and if you aren't able to collect their power within six months, the demon king will be revived. So to restore the crystal's power and prevent the world's destruction, you must befriend these seven cute girls and earn their trust... by answering trivia questions!

Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiiro-chou no Kiseki is a cross between a quiz game, a board game, and a dating simulation. Each space on the board represents a day, and the player spins a roulette to determine how many spaces to move. Each space contains various events, recovery items, or one of the girls. Meet with a girl and she'll ask you a series of trivia questions; get enough of them right and her story will continue. At the end of each month you'll face a boss battle against the demon king's minion Linz, and at the end of the game you must face the demon king himself, again as a battle of trivia questions.

The console versions of the game add proper endings for both Linz and the fairy, and also changes the names of all the characters to avoid trademark issues; it is otherwise the same game.

157147.overview:
Far in the future, humanity has spread across the galaxy, and following a long period of war, peace finally came after a treaty between the 10 great powers of the galaxy. It has been 99 years since then, and peace has prospered. On the 100th anniversary of the treaty, a new peacekeeping fleet not controlled by any one power is being established to strengthen galactic peace. But some of the nations are planning a rebellion, and the students joining this new fleet are about to be swept up in something much greater than they could have ever imagined.

QuoVadis is a turn-based isometric sci-fi war strategy game. The player controls a fleet of up to eight space warships that gradually increases in size and capability, eventually expanding to multiple fleets with different capabilities. In each mission, the player must issue commands to each ship, with the goal of defeating all enemy ships.

157148.overview:
Ten years ago, the elite officer Ovan was assigned to the president's security detail at his inauguration. Following a barely-averted assassination attempt, he attempts to track down the group responsible, but his plane is shot down and he's soon branded a traitor, wrongly accused of masterminding the attack. Forced to flee his home planet, Ovan becomes a mercenary and eventually finds and joins the group responsible for the assassination attempt, hoping to exact his revenge.

QuoVadis 2: Wakusei Kyoushuu Ovan Rei ("The Ovan Rei Planet Assault") is a sci-fi real-time strategy game. It is the sequel to QuoVadis, though the gameplay is completely different and the story is largely unrelated despite taking place in the same universe. The player commands a squad of various primary and support units, with the primary interaction being simply to direct units around the map as they will attack automatically when within range of enemies. Each mission has specific objectives such as taking control of a location or protecting certain units from attack as they travel across the map, and between missions the player can configure the loadout and characteristics of each unit in detail according to the next mission's requirement.
